text:
Sam: Heads up — saw a pronounced latency tail in staging right after the micro-interval tweak (2ms -> 1ms) + gaussian jitter enabled. Spikes ~250ms p95 on short responses. profiler attached below

Anya: Ugh, when did we roll that? Is this from the canary earlier this morning?

Sam: rolled at 03:12 UTC, small canary. The interesting bit: KV hit-rate dropped ~15% and we observed kernel hops mid-request.

Ryan: kernel hops? do you mean runtime switched execution kernels mid-generation because of seq_len bucket changes?

Sam: Yeah. Short token sequences start on the fast float16 kernel, but when batching with longer requests we sometimes promote to a fallback kernel. That causes a cache pressure window + KV eviction jitter.

Kai: Can you paste the profiler snippet? even a tiny table helps.

Sam: paste below (top lines only):
```
time_ms  | kernel         | percent
12.3     | fast_f16_attn  | 48%
18.7     | fallback_attn   | 34%  <-- hop mid-request
5.1      | kv_lookup       | 12%
2.0      | overhead         | 6%
kv_hit_rate: staging: 72%  (baseline 89%)
coalesce_delay: 1.0ms (prev 2.0ms)
jitter: gaussian sigma=0.3ms enabled
micro_interval: 1ms
```

Anya: Interesting — lower coalesce delay + smaller micro-interval increased arrival overlap so more heterogeneous sequence lengths land in the same micro-batch, forcing kernel promotion. That matches kv churn.

Ryan: Related note: token-budget gating is currently per-queue not per-microbatch, so when many tiny requests coalesce we burn through the token-budget and trigger early gating for others. Could cause the p95 to move.

Kai: So two interacting things: 1) coalesce_delay/micro_interval change -> mixed seq batches -> kernel hop -> slower kernel + more KV eviction; 2) token budget policy interacts with coalescing -> premature gating spikes.

Sam: Yep. Quick repro: run local canary with: micro_interval=1ms, coalesce_delay=0.8ms, gaussian_jitter=true, token_budget_target=1024 and hammer with 50% short (<=16) + 50% long (~512). See p95 jump.

Ryan: Suggestions? revert to micro_interval=2ms or tighten batching affinity by seq_len bucket before coalesce?

Anya: I think two-step mitigation: (A) temporarily increase coalesce_delay to 1.8-2.5ms to reduce hetero batches; (B) make token_budget gating microbatch-aware (so a single microbatch uses its own budget accounting).

Kai: Also add a cheap check: prefer kernel pinning for batches where >70% of requests are <32 tokens. Avoid mid-request kernel promotion unless unavoidable.

Sam: I can put up a hotfix PR: revert micro_interval to 2ms on staging and add a canary flag to enable kernel-pin heuristic. Will also dump a longer flamegraph to S3 for the infra team.

Ryan: +1. Can we also get a KV metric split by microbatch vs per-request to verify eviction locus? dev-bot can you create a metric ticket?

dev-bot: Created ticket INF-4127: "kv-hit-rate-by-microbatch + kernel-hop tracing" assigned to eng-runtime. Link: https://redwood.internal/t/INF-4127

Anya: Thanks. Sam — if you revert canary and attach the flamegraph link here we can triage tomorrow morning and tune token_budget targets (maybe lower to 768 for mixed workloads).

Sam: Will do. Pushed revert to staging: roll id r-2026-03-18-0318. Flamegraph -> s3://redwood-staging/perf/4601239999-flame.svg.

Kai: Nice. After revert let's run synthetic with explicit seq_len bucketing to quantify speedup and kv hit recovery.

Ryan: I'll prototype the microbatch-aware token accounting today, target PR by EOD.

Sam: Great. Thanks all. Leaving the thread open for logs; will post post-revert numbers in ~15m. :thumbsup:
